investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which are already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, causing all 4 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to be absent and the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes. Every new remote-agent pod request is rejected as Unschedulable with "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and preemption is not possible because no lower-priority victims exist. This prevents the eval runner from ever reaching the agent-creation step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is written and the contract validation fails with all 4 fields missing. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods or other workloads have consumed all allocatable VM slots, leaving no capacity for new scheduling requests. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and all three sibling check messages.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, artificially constraining the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If this selector was recently tightened or nodes were relabeled, effective capacity would have dropped. No selector change is confirmed in the supplied evidence.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if prior eval runs or user sessions did not clean up their pods, those slots remain occupied. The runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs:1883) but cleanup may not have completed if earlier runs were interrupted.

Lower confidence — cluster under-provisioning: the cluster may simply not have enough kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes for the current workload level, requiring node pool expansion rather than cleanup.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at approximately 23:21–23:26 UTC on 2026-07-05 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and the check produced zero evidence — leaving all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing and triggering a contract validation failure.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment had exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota across the two nodes that carry that resource. The remaining four nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, every remote agent pod submitted by the eval runner was stuck Unschedulable for ~144–148 seconds before the check timed out. Because agent creation never completed, the eval runner could not collect orgId, agentId, readyState, or state, causing a full contract gap. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real Kubernetes resource constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: the cluster's peer-pod VM slots are fully consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for the eval's new remote agent pod. This is the most directly supported cause given the scheduler message in failed-check.message.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod requires a specific node label or taint (e.g., a kata/peer-pod capable node pool) that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 are already at capacity. This structural constraint means even a single occupied VM slot on those nodes blocks all new remote agent pods.

Concurrent eval or workload contention: another scheduled job or live workload may have consumed the remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes just before or during the eval run window (23:21–23:26 UTC), leaving zero capacity for the probe pods.

Cluster autoscaler not configured or too slow for kata peer-pod nodes: if the node pool that carries kata.peerpods.io/vm does not autoscale, or autoscaling is too slow relative to the eval timeout (~144s), new capacity cannot be added in time to satisfy the pod.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the two kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes shows available (unallocated) VM slots at the time of the eval run, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduling or admission error should be investigated.

Consider adding a latency regression eval for remote-agent-create that alerts at warning threshold (240000ms) before the outage threshold (360000ms) is reached, providing earlier signal when scheduling is slow but not yet fully blocked.

No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; the impact is scoped to the AURA observability eval pipeline for the remote-agents feature.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which are already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, causing all 4 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to be absent and the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes. Every new remote-agent pod request is rejected as Unschedulable with "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and preemption is not possible because no lower-priority victims exist. This prevents the eval runner from ever reaching the agent-creation step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is written and the contract validation fails with all 4 fields missing. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods or other workloads have consumed all allocatable VM slots, leaving no capacity for new scheduling requests. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and all three sibling check messages.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, artificially constraining the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If this selector was recently tightened or nodes were relabeled, effective capacity would have dropped. No selector change is confirmed in the supplied evidence.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if prior eval runs or user sessions did not clean up their pods, those slots remain occupied. The runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs:1883) but cleanup may not have completed if earlier runs were interrupted.

Lower confidence — cluster under-provisioning: the cluster may simply not have enough kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes for the current workload level, requiring node pool expansion rather than cleanup.

If re-running the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and produces all 4 required evidence fields, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike) rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.
If the pod affinity/selector is found to have been recently changed to exclude 4 nodes that previously matched, the primary cause would be a configuration regression rather than capacity exhaustion.

Add a leaked-pod detection eval that lists pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and alerts if any are in a non-running or stale state beyond a configurable age threshold.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at approximately 23:21–23:26 UTC on 2026-07-05 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and the check produced zero evidence — leaving all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing and triggering a contract validation failure.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment had exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota across the two nodes that carry that resource. The remaining four nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, every remote agent pod submitted by the eval runner was stuck Unschedulable for ~144–148 seconds before the check timed out. Because agent creation never completed, the eval runner could not collect orgId, agentId, readyState, or state, causing a full contract gap. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real Kubernetes resource constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-05T23:24–23:26Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (requiring orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature in production-api has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every new remote-agent pod request times out unscheduled (~144–148 s), preventing agent creation and all downstream eval steps from executing. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; the impact is scoped to the AURA observability eval pipeline for the remote-agents feature.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) as the first substantive step; a scheduling failure here would prevent all subsequent evidence collection

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false — all three failed, indicating the shared pod-scheduling layer is the common failure point
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent or leaked remote-agent pods from prior eval runs or production workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for new scheduling requests.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource label or do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules, meaning effective capacity is limited to only 2 nodes and any saturation of those nodes causes a total scheduling blackout.

TERTIARY — Leaked or zombie pods from previous eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup: if prior eval invocations left pods running (e.g., due to a cleanup failure), those pods would hold kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and prevent new scheduling.
QUATERNARY — Cluster-level quota or LimitRange on kata.peerpods.io/vm set too low for the current eval concurrency: the quota may not have been scaled to match the number of parallel eval runs.

reproductionSteps.label: Run only the remote-agent-runtime eval probe against production-api
reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow. Expect the same Unschedulable message if capacity is still exhausted.

reproductionSteps.label: Check current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on all 6 nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Identify how many VM slots are allocatable per node and how many are currently consumed. Confirm whether the 2 eligible nodes are fully saturated.

reproductionSteps.label: List all pods currently requesting kata.peerpods.io/vm resources to identify any leaked or zombie pods
reproductionSteps.command: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.runtimeClassName=="kata" or (.metadata.annotations // {} | to_entries[] | select(.key | contains("peerpods")))) | {name: .metadata.name, ns: .metadata.namespace, phase: .status.phase}'
reproductionSteps.details: Look for pods in Pending, Running, or Unknown state that are holding VM slots from prior eval runs.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect node affinity/selector on the failing pod spec to confirm why 4 nodes are excluded
reproductionSteps.details: Verify whether the 4 excluded nodes lack the required label or resource, and whether the affinity rules are intentional.

reproductionSteps.label: Review the eval runner cleanup path in run-status-probes.mjs around the withCleanup wrapper
reproductionSteps.details: Inspect infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs near line 1916 to confirm whether withCleanup reliably deletes the agent pod on failure, and whether any prior run left pods behind.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — kata peer-pod VM scheduling layer (production-api)
affectedAreas.reason: All three remote-agents checks failed with the identical Unschedulable/Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm message, localizing the failure to the VM scheduling layer for remote agent pods in the production-api cluster.

affectedAreas.label: infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (remote-agent-runtime probe, line 1913–1918)
affectedAreas.reason: The eval runner branch for remote-agent-runtime calls createAgent with type 'remote', which triggers the kata peer-pod scheduling path. The pod never becomes schedulable, so no evidence is returned and the contract fails entirely.

affectedAreas.label: infra/evals/status/features.json (remote-agents feature registry, lines 183–185)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks registered under the remote-agents feature (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed, implicating the shared infrastructure dependency declared for this feature.

affectedAreas.label: Kubernetes cluster node pool — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity (2 eligible nodes)
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message explicitly names 2 nodes with Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes excluded by affinity/selector, confirming the capacity boundary is at the node-pool level.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity in the production-api cluster: run kubectl describe nodes and identify how many VM slots are allocated vs. available on the 2 eligible nodes.
Identify and terminate any leaked or zombie remote-agent pods from prior eval runs that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without active workloads.

If capacity is genuinely exhausted by production workloads, coordinate with the infrastructure team to scale up the kata peer-pods node pool or increase the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota on existing nodes.

Review the withCleanup path in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (around line 1916) to confirm that eval-created remote-agent pods are reliably deleted on both success and failure paths, preventing slot leakage across runs.

After restoring capacity, re-run all three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) to confirm recovery and validate that the expected-output contract evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is collected successfully.

Consider adding a pre-flight capacity check to the remote-agents eval probe that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm availability before attempting pod creation, and returns a descriptive SKIP or WARN status instead of timing out after 144+ seconds.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval probe to confirm whether scheduling failure persists
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion is ongoing or was transient. A pass on re-run would indicate the capacity was temporarily saturated; a continued fail confirms sustained exhaustion.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used on all 6 nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms whether the 2 eligible nodes are fully saturated and quantifies remaining capacity, proving or disproving the resource exhaustion hypothesis.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List all pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources to detect leaked eval pods
recommendedVerifierProbes.command: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces --field-selector=status.phase!=Succeeded,status.phase!=Failed -o wide | grep -i remote
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether prior eval runs left zombie pods consuming VM slots, which would explain why new pods cannot be scheduled.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks together to confirm shared dependency failure
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms that all three checks fail together (shared infrastructure dependency) versus independently, strengthening or weakening the shared-layer diagnosis.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect implicated eval source paths for cleanup correctness
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Verifies whether the withCleanup wrapper reliably releases kata.peerpods.io/vm slots after each eval run, and whether the feature registry and contract definitions are consistent with the current cluster configuration.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failure, resource exhaustion would be ruled out and a different scheduling constraint (e.g., a broken resource plugin or admission webhook) would need investigation.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeded without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient scheduling race or a brief quota spike rather than sustained exhaustion.

If the 4 affinity-excluded nodes were found to carry kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the affinity rules were recently changed to exclude them, the root cause would shift to a node affinity misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.

If no pods were found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of failure (i.e., the resource counter was wrong), it would point to a resource accounting bug in the kata peer-pods device plugin rather than actual saturation.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, the failure would be localized to the runtime probe logic rather than the shared scheduling layer — but the evidence shows all three failed.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check (e.g., remote-agent-node-capacity) that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used across all nodes and warns when available slots fall below a minimum threshold, providing early warning before scheduling failures occur.
Add a leaked-pod detection eval that lists remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL (e.g., 10 minutes) and fails if any are found, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust VM capacity.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector rules meets a minimum (e.g., at least 2 nodes), alerting on affinity drift before it reduces effective capacity to zero.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to capture and surface the Kubernetes scheduler event message as structured evidence when a pod fails to schedule, making future scheduling failures immediately diagnosable without manual kubectl inspection.
